independent.summary: LEO-100's build rationale claims that rolling `lastWeeklyDigestAt` back lets "the next hourly tick retry inside the same week", but `weeklyDigestDue` requires an exact UTC hour AND weekday match (`weeklyDigest.js:66-67`), and the catch-up arm that would allow an off-hour tick is explicitly LEO-084's and out of this item's scope — so the rollback can only restore *next week's* send, and an implementer following the spec would write a same-week-retry test that cannot pass.

LEO-097 states that LEO-070 owns only "length caps and the Leo-voiced 400 on POST /chat's body", but the already-filed LEO-070 explicitly says "Apply the same string checks to `GET /chat/history`'s query params" (FEATURES.md:572) — so two open Proposed items both own the type-check on `/chat/history`, and the scope boundary as written mis-states the overlap Daniel would rely on when promoting one.

grades.reason: `backend/src/services/queryGuard.js` does not exist in this tree — it is a file LEO-097 proposes creating — and a leading-space token is still a plain string that cannot match any stored `sessionToken`, so there is no bypass.

Same nonexistent file, and the proposed `requirePlainStrings` is specified to accept a value only when `typeof value === 'string'`, so an object like `{ $ne: 'x' }` fails outright — nested traversal is unnecessary.
Real pre-existing gap in `weeklyDigest.js`, but this diff touches only FEATURES.md and is the change that *files* it as LEO-100 defect (1), so it is not a defect of this change.

Also a real pre-existing behaviour (headline pushed unconditionally at line 197) that this diff does not touch and in fact files as LEO-100 defect (2); duplicating the item's own text is not a review finding.
Correct about the existing stamp-before-send ordering, but again untouched by this FEATURES.md-only diff and already filed verbatim as LEO-100 defect (3).

The renewal is exactly what the item mandates — a verbatim copy at the bottom of Block L with the next free id and `[not-before: run date 2026-10-15 + 7 = 2026-10-22]` — so the tag is compliance, not a mismatch.
